title: Deterministic source parsing and exact-SKU candidate resolution
summary: Build the tier-zero parser for source wording, SKU candidates, unit/pack reconciliation, numeric ordering, attachment gating, and explicit unresolved output before any model or commercial command is considered.
steps: Parse source text and readable attachments into versioned token, candidate, unit, pack, and uncertainty facts.
Match only tenant-authorized SKU/alias candidates and retain alternative candidates plus matching evidence.
Stop at explicit unresolved state when a unit, attachment, source, or product distinction cannot be reconciled.

positive: A clean exact-SKU/compatible-unit input yields a reproducible structured proposal with source spans.
negative: An unread attachment, ambiguous variant, unrecognized unit, or missing price cannot become a fabricated line, total, or outbound answer.

doneConditions: Deterministic parser cases cover accents, aliases, variants, pack/unit mismatch, numeric sort, attachments, and unknown values.
requiredEvidence: Parser corpus result, source-span trace, and unresolved-case regression set.

title: Bounded reasoning, prediction, and constrained reply path
summary: Run approved intelligence only through versioned releases and authorized command/proposal envelopes, producing bounded finished-albarán predictions or reply drafts with evidence, alternatives, cost, and human/tenant grant policy.
steps: Construct minimized, tenant-authorized context from retained evidence and versioned release policy.
Persist run, model/prompt/release version, input evidence hash, budget decision, candidate output, alternatives, and outcome.
Convert accepted intelligence only into explicit proposal or command routes; external reply requires separate policy and provider evidence.

positive: A permitted approved release creates a reviewable prediction or reply draft with exact evidence and version lineage.
negative: A model cannot auto-issue, reprice, alter stock, resolve a concern, send externally, or claim an unavailable provider succeeded.

doneConditions: Prediction/reply tests cover release allowlist, grant denial, budget denial, cancellation, stale input, and source-evidence inspection.
requiredEvidence: Frozen-release evaluation trace, budget decision record, and denied-mutation test.

title: Intelligence concerns, explanation, and human review lifecycle
summary: Specify observable scoped concern UI: one exact target, one red boundary, a concise dismissible reason, local re-evaluation after relevant edit or sent message, and retained disclosure history. Durable storage, model evaluation and learning remain later seams.
steps: Define one exact UI target: message/email card, field, full product row or contiguous row group; use one red boundary and a short dismissible colleague-style explanation immediately above it.
Re-evaluate only a relevant edited or sent-message scope; resolve, replace or dismiss stale reply notes with optional brief acknowledgement while retaining earlier local history.
Use the same scope/reason/lifecycle in full Albarán, condensed order-in-chat and composer tray; do not imply a provider, model or outbound action.

positive: A dismissed concern remains auditable and can reopen when its source/policy changes.
negative: A generic rating, confidence score, or unscoped model explanation cannot override a commercial or source fact.

doneConditions: Concern scope, lifecycle, visibility, accessibility, and no-direct-mutation tests are green.
requiredEvidence: Concern audit history, policy-change reopen test, and explanation source-link trace.

title: Interactive catalogue and variant intelligence
summary: Deliver an interactive, review-first catalogue intelligence surface for category feedback, variant interpretation, corrected descriptions, alternatives, and injection-safe conversation state.
steps: Scope the interaction to tenant-authorized catalogue records and source evidence with a bounded release/tool policy.
Return proposal, alternatives, missing facts, original wording, evidence, and review actions rather than direct record mutations.
Treat untrusted source text as data and prevent it from overriding instructions, authority, or tenant scope.

positive: A reviewer can correct a proposed classification or variant description and see the revisioned proposal change.
negative: Conversation text cannot grant capabilities, alter policy, create a sellable SKU, or publish a category change without review.

doneConditions: Interactive proposal, alternative, correction, injection-safety, permission, and failure-state tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Proposal review trace, adversarial input suite, and scoped interaction transcript fixture.

title: Evaluation, replay, trace export, and error analysis
summary: Create consent/retention-eligible test sets, chronological replay, frozen release evaluation, metrics, error slices, trace export, and a release gate that reports uncertainty honestly.
steps: Register dataset consent, retention, tenant/test lineage, date boundaries, and task-specific expected outcomes.
Replay inputs chronologically against frozen releases and capture evidence, decision, abstention, cost, latency, and error class.
Export redacted traces under authorization and require a reviewed metric definition before making performance claims.

positive: A release report states dataset, version, abstentions, error slices, and exact evidence for each claimed metric.
negative: A design demo, unversioned prompt, future context, raw customer text, or ambiguous denominator cannot become an accuracy claim.

doneConditions: Dataset governance, replay chronology, trace-redaction, metric-definition, and regression-gate tests are recorded.
requiredEvidence: Evaluation manifest, frozen replay report, and redacted trace export test.

title: Authorized backfill, correction learning, and model recovery
summary: Backfill approved source-to-record links and learning inputs through resumable, reviewable, tenant-safe jobs that preserve historical facts and never promote a correction merely because it repeats.
steps: Select only policy-eligible source/record pairs and record selection criteria, release, actor, and approval.
Run bounded idempotent backfill chunks with proposal/review outputs and no direct historical rewrite.
Supersede or retract dependent proposals when correction/source provenance changes.

positive: A resumed backfill returns the same request/proposal IDs and reports reviewed versus pending results.
negative: Repeated wording, retrospective model output, or a failed job cannot rewrite issued documents, stock, price, or source history.

doneConditions: Backfill eligibility, resume, correction supersession, retention, and no-historical-rewrite tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Backfill checkpoint trace, proposal supersession audit, and historical replay regression.

title: Illustration library, reference audit, and SKU association model
summary: Keep the approved image library, visual aliases, reference audit, asset checksum, source/license metadata, and SKU-owned association distinct from tenant catalogue identity and Internal-category/group or Related-items presentation.
steps: Register immutable asset checksum, source/provider, review state, permitted use, and visual alias without asserting taxonomy or SKU membership.
Attach a reviewed association to each SKU independently, allowing byte deduplication without approval inheritance.
Keep any optional Internal-category/group or Related-items presentation art labelled separately from item identity and assignment.

positive: An approved library asset can be associated to one reviewed SKU with retained provenance and unchanged SKU identity.
negative: A visual alias, reference class, Internal-category/group or Related-items presentation, or generic fallback cannot add a SKU or automatically approve a variant image.

doneConditions: Library/association/alias/Internal-category/group or Related-items presentation and provenance tests are green.
requiredEvidence: Asset association audit, checksum validation, and variant non-inheritance test.

title: Budgeted asynchronous image generation worker
summary: Implement a provider-isolated image request worker with reviewed description, prompt/style version/hash, SKU revision, budget authorization, idempotency, job lifecycle, provider receipt, timeout, retry, cancel, and dead-letter handling.
steps: Deduplicate requests by tenant/SKU/revision/visual-description/prompt-version and authorize budget before provider submission.
Persist requested, validated, submitted, receipt, candidate, review, approved/rejected, failed, cancelled, and stale states.
Validate returned bytes and reference constraints before a candidate can enter review.

positive: A valid authorized request produces one durable job and captures the provider receipt only after it exists.
negative: A local request, absent credential, duplicate retry, malformed asset, over-budget call, or provider failure cannot publish or claim generation success.

doneConditions: Mock-provider idempotency, budget, timeout, cancellation, malformed-image, and dead-letter tests pass before any paid proof.
requiredEvidence: Job state-machine trace, mock receipt fixture, and budget-denial test.

title: Image candidate review, publication, and replacement recovery
summary: Review image candidates for SKU form, packaging, brand, safety, and source policy before assignment; retain last approved art during replacement and keep all decisions auditable.
steps: Validate upload type/size/scan/quarantine and bind candidates to exact tenant/SKU/revision.
Require reviewer authority, decision, reason, and content/provenance gate before association update.
Keep approved asset visible while a requested/candidate/failed replacement is pending and preserve archive restrictions.

positive: An approved candidate replaces only its reviewed SKU association and creates an auditable revision.
negative: An upload, generated candidate, archived SKU, or family image cannot assign itself or erase the previous approved asset.

requiredEvidence: Artwork review audit, upload quarantine test, and last-approved fallback test.

title: Messaging integration, inbound source rail, and future outbound receipt boundary
summary: Implement a provider adapter for verified inbound messaging, per-tenant connection ownership, test isolation, capability checks, and revoke behavior. The full production outbound receipt boundary remains specified, but the order-review profile enables only native WhatsApp handoff and never offers customer send, template, queue, or delivery claims.
steps: Verify origin, signature, replay window, schema, mapping, and idempotency before source retention.
Route the order-review profile through no-outbound transport and native-provider handoff; a future live send requires its own explicit tenant grant/policy and release-profile enablement.
When outbound is separately enabled, record delivery request, provider submission, receipt, failure, retry, and reconciliation as distinct auditable facts.

Bind messaging connection capability to the named tenant line and assigned salesperson; setup displays pending/unavailable separately from verified provider capability and does not confuse inbound access with outbound permission.

positive: A verified authorised inbound line records its owner and native handoff boundary without widening customer scope.
When separately enabled, an authorized live send becomes delivered only after a matching provider receipt/reconciliation state.
negative: A browser test, inbound connection, reply-attention tray, queued reply, or missing receipt cannot send externally or display delivered.
A configured line, browser test or unavailable provider cannot claim a live send or verified connection; in order review, no customer outbound control is enabled.

doneConditions: Webhook, tenant mapping, test isolation, revoke, duplicate, provider-outage, native-handoff, and no-outbound order-review tests pass; full outbound receipt tests remain required before that capability is enabled.
requiredEvidence: Mock webhook verification, order-review no-outbound/native-handoff trace, and future delivery receipt reconciliation report.

title: Mailbox authorization, source sync, native handoff, and future document delivery
summary: Connect authorized mailboxes through a provider-neutral OAuth/callback flow, ingest source safely, scope visibility, and provide native Outlook/Gmail handoff. Full document-mail delivery remains separately specified; the order-review profile sends no customer email and does not retain source email bodies/files as a substitute mailbox.
steps: Store opaque connection references, grants, scope, tenant mapping, expiry, and callback state without exposing provider secrets.
Ingest accepted message/attachment sources through a source envelope, preserve connection/cursor provenance, and open the relevant native provider for the operator; original custody remains external.

When separately enabled, send document mail through selected saved-copy revision/recipient policy and distinguish accepted job from provider receipt. A scheduled subcontractor order-list email is a first-class, independently gated Export delivery: its schedule object carries recipient rule, attachment/template, connection profile, next run, history and explicit edit/pause/remove actions; Send history is outside the editor. Final rendered draft and unusual/new change note are reviewed pre-send seams only; any AI proposal/runtime remains deferred. It is not customer messaging.

positive: A permitted mailbox sync advances a cursor only after durable accepted source processing, and the order-review surface can return the operator to the matching native provider thread.
negative: An expired, revoked, unscoped, or failed authorization cannot expose mailbox data, retain original bodies/files as a local mailbox, claim document delivery, or enable customer email in order review.

doneConditions: OAuth state, scope, callback, sync cursor, revoke, provider-error and native-handoff paths are tested; receipt tests remain required before separately enabled delivery.
requiredEvidence: Authorized callback/native-handoff trace, cursor reconciliation report, revoked-connection denial test, and separately gated document/subcontractor-delivery receipt trace.

title: ERP integration adapters, reconciliation, and manual recovery
summary: Use versioned adapter profiles to export/reconcile authorized document and catalogue snapshots with cadence, cursor, conflict, receipt, retry, and manual repair semantics.
steps: Model adapter capability, schema/profile version, cadence, cursor, reconciliation key, and per-record attempt.
Send immutable snapshots under explicit tenant/connection authority and record accepted/external/reconciled divergence states.
Provide pause, retry, resync, manual repair proposal, and disable/revoke actions with no silent overwrite.
Resolve a selected product-option policy to a declared ERP line representation only after approved mapping; retain the base-item/note default and surface missing destination support for review.

positive: A reconciliation report identifies matching, pending, rejected, and divergent records by stable IDs and revision.
An approved mapped variation yields an attributable adapter request whose source SKU, approved mapping, policy revision and returned receipt remain independently traceable.
negative: A queue, cursor advance, generic CSV, or provider availability cannot be represented as ERP synchronization.
A UI select, recurring note, absent mapping or provider timeout cannot create an ERP item, silently substitute a line, claim sync completion or erase the source/approval distinction.

doneConditions: Profile validation, external duplicate prevention, cursor, conflict, retry, and reconciliation tests pass.
JNY-P02 has approved-mapping, base-item-note default, missing-mapping, adapter-denial and provider-receipt tests.
requiredEvidence: Adapter contract fixture, reconciliation report, and failure/retry audit trace.
ERP adapter contract trace showing base-item-note fallback is explicit and mapped variation is rejected without approved mapping.

title: Maps and place-provider adapter
summary: Integrate geocoding/place suggestions through a tenant-policy-aware adapter with limited data, manual fallback, provider health, and no automatic address or route commitment.
steps: Request only permitted address fields through a constrained provider adapter.
Store provider result/availability separately from the customer-approved address and route policy.
Offer manual entry/correction and explain unavailable, denied, quota, and stale state without external details.

positive: A user can save a valid manual address when the provider is unavailable.
negative: A suggestion, map pin, or failed lookup cannot change a customer address, delivery promise, or route without confirmation.

doneConditions: Provider, manual fallback, privacy minimization, quota/error, and address-confirmation tests pass.
requiredEvidence: Places adapter contract test and manual-fallback state trace.

title: Connection registry, health, reconciliation, and revoke controls
summary: Operate every external rail through a tenant-owned connection registry with capability, credential reference, test, health, queue, cursor, receipt, pause, revoke, and incident state.
steps: Register connection owner, tenant, opaque credential reference, scopes, enabled capability, policy, and test lineage.
Expose configured, authorizing, ready, degraded, paused, revoked, failed, stale, and unknown states with last known evidence.
Stop new external work on revoke/pause and preserve prior receipts/audit for recovery.

positive: A revoked connection immediately rejects a new external job while keeping historic receipt evidence readable.
negative: A configured card, health ping, stale cursor, or generic success badge cannot imply a functioning authorized rail.

doneConditions: Connection setup/test/pause/revoke/health/reconciliation and permission tests are complete for each enabled rail.
requiredEvidence: Connection registry audit, revoke-denial test, and health/reconciliation trace.

title: Operator assistant, availability incidents and reviewed customer updates
summary: Deliver the full tenant assistant with its own history, additive dictation, scoped supply/category proposals, reviewed affected orders and exact outbound payloads, and per-recipient receipt/recovery.
steps: Persist authorized authored conversation history, typed evidence/proposal/approval/tool summaries and retention/redaction state separately from provider-owned incoming raw mail/files.
Implement UTL-A01–A04 launch/context/history/composer/dictation and exact product/problem/availability/when report; preserve underlying customer chat draft.

Implement UTL-A05 impact projection from confirmed operator report or current ledger/source evidence without mutating physical stock; unknown equivalence and no-affected-order states stay useful and honest.

For Review stock, suspend the assistant while retaining its saved report, publish one exact-SKU count intent, then use the product door to mount that SKU sheet before it consumes the intent; this handoff must work on phone as well as desktop and Back/reopen must restore the report.
Implement UTL-A06–A09 immutable recipient/copy review, digest/revision approval, authorized delivery, per-recipient dispositions, reconciliation and retry of only eligible failures.
Implement UTL-A10–A12 explicit classification before/after command, incident reevaluation/lifecycle and reopened conversation recovery; no stale approval reuse.

Wire approved versioned LLM/tool release and dictation adapters with budget/timeout/cancel/eval controls; manual review remains available when unconnected, and the browser kit must never present structured prompts, manual review text or local UI as real model generation or delivery.

positive: An operator can report a new shortage not present in the old ledger, review exact affected orders and customer wording, and observe real partial delivery outcomes.
A category discussion can apply only reviewed classification relationships while all commercial SKU facts remain unchanged.
A phone or desktop Review stock handoff reaches the exact SKU count editor and a reopened assistant thread restores the retained report.
A timeout or incomplete provider receipt is reconciled under its original identity before any new send.
negative: A report, model/tool message, dictation result, preview or local successful-looking UI cannot change stock, approve itself, send to customers or fabricate a provider receipt.
In an unconnected kit, a composer response, evidence trail or manual proposal cannot be labelled as an LLM result, generated customer message or transport outcome.
A changed recipient/text/order/policy revision invalidates approval; an accepted or unknown recipient cannot be blindly retried.
Assistant history, raw mail/files or contact cards cannot cross tenant boundaries or authorize broader access.

doneConditions: Every UTL-A control passes empty/loading/permission/offline/dirty/reopen/concurrent/stale/unknown and narrow-screen states.
Recorded incident → impact → proposal → approval → per-recipient attempt trace is reproducible with current policy/units and adversarial source fixtures.
No live-send or model-execution claim until the exact provider adapter has its own controlled and operational evidence.
requiredEvidence: Tenant-isolation and prompt-injection suite; seven-order/new-shortage, no-impact, missing conversion, partial receipt, timeout reconciliation and stale-approval traces.
Assistant/customer/support mutual-context and draft/focus/history browser proof; dictation append/cancel/typing-race test.
Provider receipt schema, exact payload digest and idempotency reconciliation contract tests, retention/deletion and operator runbook.
